title: Dodge and Burn: Black-and-White Landscape Post-Processing with Clone-Paint and Sky/Wave Compositing

date.basis: embedded_creation_time metadata; approximate export date inferred from file metadata

summary: This landscape post-processing workflow centers on creating a dramatic black-and-white image through selective dodging and burning, while using clone-painting techniques to stabilize texture and blend foreground, waves, sky, and added elements. The instructor argues for retaining color information in the file to visualize tonal relationships and demonstrates how dehaze, curves, and noise-management steps can be leveraged in RAW to craft a powerful sky. The video then guides through composition decisions (space for side-light), perspective adjustments, heavy emphasis on the heart of B&W work (dodging/burning), and culminates in a composite workflow that adds an iceberg and diffuse sky elements to enhance depth and three-dimensionality.

sections.title: Introduction to black-and-white post-processing and the role of dodge and burn
concepts: retaining color information in the file
sections.description: The presenter explains why many retain color data when converting to black and white to visualize tonal relationships, and positions dodge and burn as the core method for shaping light and tone without relying on dedicated B&W software. The discussion also touches on how working in RGB while black-and-white can enhance tonal separation.

sections.title: Sky handling, dehaze, curves, and initial sky preparation
sections.description: The workflow covers using dehaze to dramatically improve a sky (with notes on its adverse color effects if used aggressively in color). It also covers applying curves to control lights and darks, preparing foreground and sky separately, and managing noise by selective luminance noise reduction on the sky region.

sections.title: The heart of B&W processing: dodge and burn to sculpt light
sections.description: This section is presented as the core technique—extensive dodge-and-burn to shape light, mid-tones, shadows, and highlights across the scene. The instructor emphasizes the direction of light, side-light concepts, and the goal of achieving a natural yet three-dimensional look, with an emphasis on practice and developing an artistic eye.

sections.title: Perspective, composition tweaks, and iceberg composite
sections.description: The final portion covers compositional adjustments to emphasize side-light by adding space to the anticipated light source, using perspective warp to refine the frame without sacrificing quality, and introducing an iceberg composite with sky diffusion to integrate new elements and enhance depth and atmosphere.
